entities.summary: Deal Castle is an artillery fort constructed by Henry VIII in Deal, Kent, between 1539 and 1540. It formed part of the King's Device programme to protect against invasion from France and the Holy Roman Empire, and defended the strategically important Downs anchorage off the English coast. Comprising a keep with six inner and outer bastions, the moated stone castle covered 0.85 acres (0.34 ha) and had sixty-six firing positions for artillery. It cost the Crown a total of £27,092 to build the three castles of Deal, Sandown and Walmer, which lay adjacent to one another along the coast and were connected by earthwork defences.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Deal Castle played a significant regional role as part of Henry VIII's King's Device programme to protect against invasion from France and the Holy Roman Empire. The construction of these three castles along the English coast, including Deal Castle, cost £27,092 and had sixty-six firing positions for artillery.
